statement: Let V(root) be the set of all values that occur at some node of root. The function returns a result r and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), letting q = queries[i]: len(r) = len(queries); len(r[i]) = 2; if the set {x in V(root) | x <= q} is nonempty then r[i][0] is its maximum, otherwise r[i][0] = -1; and if the set {x in V(root) | x >= q} is nonempty then r[i][1] is its minimum, otherwise r[i][1] = -1.
preconditions: root is a binary search tree (its in-order traversal of node values is nondecreasing), root has between 2 and 100000 nodes inclusive, every node value is in [1, 1000000], queries is a slice with 1 <= len(queries) <= 100000, and every entry queries[i] satisfies 1 <= queries[i] <= 1000000 for all 0 <= i < len(queries).
